acceptance: Red test first: a protected-path blocker that cites a frozen predicate file (go/acs/cycle<N>/predicates_test.go) and the conflicting TDD predicate is accepted when the cited line exists and the frozen-check gate flags that path.
A blocker that cites a test file the lane may edit is still refused.
An accepted protected-path blocker routes the item to the console with the builder's patch attached, instead of failing the cycle.
fix: The blocker proof refuses every blocker whose cited file is a test file ('is not a non-test Go source file in the tree'). Cycles 2073 and 2089 (wave 147-148) declared correct blockers on protected acs predicates (a TDD predicate that can never pass; a frozen predicate that calls a removed API) and both were refused, so the cycle spent its build retries and failed. Accept a protected-path blocker on a frozen or this-cycle acs predicate when the cited line exists and the gate classifier flags the path, and route the item to the console with the patch.
notes: Console route: orchestrator blocker proof. Find the refusal with grep 'is not a non-test Go source file'.
summary: A correct protected-path blocker on an acs predicate is always refused, so a lane that hits a frozen or impossible predicate burns its retries and fails.
title: The blocker proof accepts a protected-path blocker on an acs predicate and routes the item to the console
